lesson_title: Paper 1 Practice Run: Finance and Data at Examination Pace
hook_text: The exam paper's shape NEVER changes. Most people walk in without the map.
clip_script: Paper 1, Mathematical Literacy: 150 marks, and its shape never changes. Question 1: thirty marks of Level 1 only — VAT on R240 is R36, net pay is gross minus deductions, done. That's your warm-up lap, banked. Question 2, Finance — and here's the water bill that catches thousands. First 6 kilolitres free, next block R18, top block R26. The house used 22. Do NOT charge all 22 at the top rate — the tariff is a staircase. Free 6, then 9 times 18 is 162, then 7 times 26 is 182. Subtotal 344, times 1,15 for VAT: R395,60. Six marks, one per stair. Now the secret the memo keeps: consistent accuracy. Slip on one stair? Carry your wrong number forward and keep the operations clean — every later step still pays. An abandoned question pays nothing, ever. And read the mark allocation like an instruction: two marks, one line. Six marks, show the staircase. Comment questions? A sentence with a computed number inside it — the mean is 59 BUT a quarter of the class sits below 49. Numbers plus because equals marks. Walk the whole paper once at exam pace and the real thing becomes your second rehearsal.
visual_style: An exam paper unfolding into a floor-plan-style map of five questions; a water tariff drawn as a literal staircase with rand amounts stacking per step; a red slip mark flowing forward through green ticks; a mark-allocation dial translating (2), (4), (6) into line counts.
pacing: Fast opening map, deliberate slow-down on the staircase bill, punchy consistent-accuracy reveal, quick-fire closing habits.
call_to_action: Watch the full practice run and sit Paper 1 like it's your third time seeing it.
